name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,275

clue.text: Unfortunate daughter falling over sink

indicators.note: something falling over ends up upside down, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
poor in the sense of unlucky, as in 'poor thing'

explanation.surface: A sad tale of an unlucky daughter who falls over a kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunate' is placed first to look like an adjective for the daughter, but its synonym comes second and flips. D plus ROOP gives DROOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or hang down, a close verbal synonym of sink in the sense of drooping flowers or spirits.

clue.text: Craze given up over time — it’s crazy

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word up means reading it from the bottom, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a fad is a short-lived craze
T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a passing craze after a while and admits it was mad all along.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the reversed craze sits on top of the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is informal British for silly or foolish, a close synonym of crazy used as an adjective.

clue.text: Has topless items of clothing

indicators.note: without a top, so the first letter of the word is lost

blocks.note: gowns are dresses or robes

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone possessing clothing that leaves the top half bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests a garment style, but it removes the G from GOWNS to leave OWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, so the verb works as a direct synonym of has in the third person.

clue.text: Writer questions entertaining company in Sunday feast

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside the house, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a common crossword writer
a test is a set of questions; to test is to question
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An author grills a group of guests over a big Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer questions' reads as a subject and verb, but each word is its own piece; the container goes into the middle of the second piece, not around the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, also called Whit Sunday, is a Christian festival held on the seventh Sunday after Easter.

clue.text: Struck deals, about 2000, after comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return journey, so the word is read coming back the other way
about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for 1000, so two of them make 2000

explanation.surface: A business story: agreements signed around the year 2000, after a company's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struck deals' reads as one phrase about making agreements, but 'Struck' is the definition alone. SLAED wraps MM.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam is to hit or bang hard, so the past tense matches struck as in striking a blow.

clue.text: Second drink — gosh! — like sex on the beach?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
tea is a drink
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise like 'gosh!'

explanation.surface: Ordering a second cocktail, a Sex on the Beach, with a gasp of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Sex on the Beach is a cocktail, which the 'drink' plants in the mind; here the phrase is taken literally, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes erotic or passionate scenes, and an amorous encounter on hot sand would be both erotic and hot.

clue.text: Attach a couple of diamonds

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds, and a couple is two

explanation.surface: Setting a pair of diamonds into a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The jewellery picture hides the card-suit abbreviation D for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To add something is to join or append it to what is already there, so it matches attach as a verb.

clue.text: I’m aching to travel somewhere in America

indicators.note: letters that travel move about and land in new positions

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone longing to take a trip to a US destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aching to travel' reads as yearning to go somewhere, but 'to travel' tells you to scramble the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Michigan is a US state in the Great Lakes region, so it is one example of a place in America.

clue.text: Footballer put off letting goal in

indicators.note: letting something in means allowing it inside, so one piece admits another

blocks.note: to defer is to postpone
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A footballer is discouraged after letting in a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' is not a football goal but an aim or purpose; 'letting' and 'in' together frame the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is a player positioned at the back whose job is stopping the opposing team from scoring.

clue.text: Provide money for African party when it’s sunny outside

indicators.note: one piece sits outside another, wrapping around it

blocks.note: fine weather is sunny weather
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Funding a political party's event held outdoors when the weather is good.
explanation.walkthrough: The outdoor party is a political one, not a celebration; the ANC is South Africa's governing party.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a project is to fund it, supplying the capital or cash that it needs.

clue.text: Wilfully reluctant to hear about cold coffee

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: as in turning a deaf ear, refusing to listen
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly refusing to listen to complaints about their cold coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests 'cold coffee' is iced coffee; the C is one letter and 'coffee' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is the short informal name for decaffeinated coffee, one kind of coffee drink.

clue.text: Official approval for a church campaign?

blocks.note: per means for each, as in 'a pound per head'
a mission is a church's organised campaign of evangelism

explanation.surface: A church seeks formal sanction before launching a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'for a' is to be read as the Latin-derived PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission is authorisation or consent granted by someone in authority, which is what official approval means.

clue.text: Tricky issue with cats — they need to be packed for journeys

definitions.text: they need to be packed for journeys

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The awkward problem of pets that have to come along on every trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'they' seem to be the cats; it refers to the answer instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitcases are luggage cases filled with clothes before travel, so they are items people pack for trips.

clue.text: A measure to install valve only if absolutely necessary

indicators.note: installing something puts it inside, so one piece is fitted into another

blocks.note: taken as written
an inch is a measure of length
a tap is a valve controlling flow

explanation.surface: A plumber's rule: fit a new valve only when there is no other choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A measure' is split: the A stands alone and the measure is the unit, with the valve fitted between them.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch is an idiom meaning in an emergency or if forced, when nothing better is available.

clue.text: Idolising criminal group, always getting taken in

indicators.note: something taken in is received inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Hero-worship of a gang, whose admirers are forever being duped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being fooled, but here it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Revering means holding in deep respect or awe, the same as idolising someone as a hero.

clue.text: Some get remorseful and shake

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is a portion of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Some people feel guilty and start trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like 'some people' but it points at a run of letters in geT REMORseful.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is an involuntary quivering, so as a noun it is a shake or tremble.

clue.text: Buccaneer quiet, then angry

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
irate means angry

explanation.surface: A sea robber who goes silent before flying into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quiet comes from the musical marking piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a seventeenth-century sea raider of the Caribbean, which makes the word a synonym.

clue.text: Jerky movement as bird lands on church

blocks.note: a wren is a small songbird
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bird twitches as it alights on a church roof.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lands on' means sits above, so the bird comes before CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden violent twist or pull, which is a jerky movement.

clue.text: Top courier on the move in Caribbean island

indicators.note: letters on the move shift position into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A star delivery rider out on the job in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as an adjective praising the courier; its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerto Rico is an island territory of the United States in the Caribbean Sea, east of Hispaniola.

clue.text: Left little devil unable to function properly

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an imp is a small devil

explanation.surface: An abandoned little devil that cannot work properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb meaning abandoned, but it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means floppy, weak and lacking strength, so something limp cannot work or perform as it should.

clue.text: A good artist in an Indian city

blocks.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A talented painter living in a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link here, not a container signal: the three pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in Uttar Pradesh in northern India, famous as the site of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Clamour is evident in Christmas endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is dropped
to be evident in something is to show up inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
taken as written

explanation.surface: The racket of the festive season seems never to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' does double duty in the surface as a verb, but it is literally the two letters placed inside the shortened festive word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamour is loud, confused shouting or din, and noise is the general word for such sound.

clue.text: Sin admitted by Father Riley

indicators.note: what is admitted is let inside, so the answer sits within the following words

blocks.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A priest named Riley confesses a misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The confessional picture of a priest admitting sin disguises a run of letters in fathER Riley.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake or do wrong, so the verb works as a synonym of sin.

clue.text: Like many a bird, one releasing egg — smart!

indicators.note: releasing something means letting it go, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: taken as written
an egg is round, like the letter O
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: A bird laying an egg, with a cry of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird picture makes 'releasing egg' sound like laying; here O is dropped from ONE to leave NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Many birds in spring are busy building nests and sitting on them, so they are described as nesting.

clue.text: He painted pig and hart in motion

indicators.note: letters in motion move around and settle in a new order

blocks.note: a hog is a pig
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist painted a pig and a deer mid-stride.
explanation.walkthrough: A hart is a male deer; its letters are rearranged after HOG. William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth was a celebrated English painter and engraver, known for The Rake's Progress, so he is a man who painted.

clue.text: Brown primates circling round island

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is written backwards
circling means going around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: apes are primates
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Brown monkeys swim around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like it describes the primates, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment originally from cuttlefish ink, familiar from old photographs.
